reason: The text extensively demonstrates that agency is not limited to leaders. The people of Israel exercise significant collective agency throughout the narrative: they petition Rehoboam to lighten their burden (וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם), deliberately reject his rule, actively summon and install Jeroboam as king (וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ), and orchestrate a successful rebellion. Additionally, Jeroboam exercises consequential agency as a servant before becoming king. Individual prophets and other non-leadership figures also demonstrate autonomous agency in the narrative. The people's actions fundamentally shape the political outcome, proving agency is distributed across the social hierarchy.
